nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration/testing fees and sandbox usage
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling/licences and extract environment
Staging/CI infrastructure (cloud costs for pipeline, staging env, observability stack)
Third-party accessibility audit (WCAG 2.2 AA certification support)
Contingency buffer (~10% of labour) for scope uncertainty and integration risk

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based on backlog points and role rate card only.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 effective hours of blended team effort, adjusted per task type (integration/migration tasks weighted higher due to risk).
Backend Developer capacity is 1.5 FTE (~2,400 hrs over a ~6 month delivery window at 40hrs/wk/FTE); allocated 1,900 hrs leaves headroom for code review, bug fixing and support tasks not itemized.

Frontend Developer is only 1.0 FTE (~1,600 hrs over 6 months); backlog has heavy frontend content (design system, dashboard, invoice UI, accessibility, mobile, admin back-office) so 1,500 hrs is a tight but feasible allocation — this role is a likely bottleneck.
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (~960 hrs available) is allocated 700 hrs, concentrated on Urgent/High priority items (auth, RBAC, payments, migration) with lighter regression coverage on Low priority items.

DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE (~640 hrs available) is allocated 350 hrs, focused on CI/CD setup, observability, and legacy decommission; this role is thinly staffed relative to backlog needs (migration infra, observability, decommission) and may need contractor support if timeline compresses.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) assumed to require significant Backend + DevOps time due to schema mapping, volume (400k records/2M invoice lines) and validation/reconciliation.
Payment integration (PW-7) assumed to include webhook handling, reconciliation logic and PCI-adjacent testing, driving above-average QA hours.
Multi-currency (PW-14) assumed to require ongoing FX rate feed integration, not just static conversion.
Delivery timeline assumed to be approximately 6 months given available FTE capacity; if compressed, additional contract staff would be needed at extra cost not reflected here.
Non-labour costs are estimates based on typical SaaS tooling/cloud spend for a project of this scale; actual vendor quotes were not available.
Contingency of ~10% on labour cost is included to cover estimation uncertainty given no historical actuals exist.
input.reasoning: Backlog was translated to hours by weighting story points by task complexity/risk (integration, migration and security-sensitive tasks weighted above simple CRUD/UI tasks) and mapping to the four staffed roles per task type (backend-heavy: auth, RBAC, payments, migration, audit log, rate limiting; frontend-heavy: design system, dashboard, invoice UI, accessibility, mobile, admin UI, analytics; QA across all Urgent/High items plus regression; DevOps for CI/CD, observability, decommission). Total allocated hours were checked against each role's FTE capacity over an assumed ~6 month delivery window to flag under/over-staffing risk — Frontend and DevOps are the tightest constraints. Priority breakdown allocates cost proportionally to the backlog items in each priority bucket, weighted by their point-implied effort. Three scenarios (P20/P50/P80) reflect the spread between a smooth delivery (optimistic), the base-case plan as costed, and a pessimistic case incorporating migration/integration rework and QA cycles overrunning given how thin QA and DevOps capacity are relative to backlog breadth. No actuals exist, so confidence is medium at best on the most-likely case and low on the pessimistic tail.

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff, Low priority, 13 pts) to a future phase; support staff can use existing DB tooling short-term.
reductions.effect: Removes an entire feature from Frontend/Backend/QA scope, freeing ~230 hrs across roles.

reductions.description: Defer PW-19 (Usage analytics and reporting, Low priority, 8 pts) and PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API, Low priority, 5 pts) to post-launch backlog.
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend/Frontend/QA hours by ~150 hrs combined; both are Low priority and not launch-critical.

reductions.description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14, 13 pts) scope to USD+EUR only at launch, adding PLN later.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~70 hrs of Backend/QA effort on FX edge cases and settlement logic testing.

reductions.description: Use a managed/off-the-shelf audit logging library instead of building PW-10 (Audit log) from scratch.
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend hours by ~60 hrs by leveraging existing tooling instead of custom append-only store implementation.

reductions.description: Defer legacy portal decommission (PW-24, Low priority, 8 pts) until 2-3 months after go-live once traffic has migrated.
reductions.effect: Removes ~40 DevOps + Backend hours from the initial delivery window; DevOps is the most capacity-constrained role.

reductions.description: Skip the third-party accessibility audit and rely on internal QA/manual review against WCAG 2.2 AA checklist.
reductions.effect: Removes external non-labour spend; slightly increases risk of missed edge cases but reduces direct cost.
